sources.title: OpenCode README
sources.locator: Overview, setup, features and component boundaries
sources.finding: OpenCode provides terminal and desktop installs, describes desktop beta and built-in agent modes. The current source distribution uses MIT; desktop packaging and provider access have separate docs.

sources.title: OpenCode desktop
sources.finding: Desktop clients support concurrent sessions, diffs, line comments and a browser. Terminal persistence is documented in v2.2.4 notes.

sources.title: OpenCode Mobile
sources.finding: iPhone TestFlight client pairs to the user computer; Android is coming soon. Pairing links are one-use and expire in five minutes.

sources.title: OpenCode providers
sources.finding: Documents provider credentials, ChatGPT Plus/Pro, custom compatible endpoints, transport timeouts and three retries.

sources.title: OpenCode agents
sources.finding: Primary and child sessions have named profiles, model settings and independent permission rules. Steps can bound a model run.

sources.title: OpenCode CLI
sources.finding: CLI run supports scripted prompts. A shared background server owns local sessions and survives client UI lifetime.

sources.title: OpenCode JavaScript client
sources.locator: Create a client; Stream events; Local background service
sources.finding: Typed HTTP client creates and prompts sessions; event streams have no replay or automatic reconnection.

sources.title: OpenCode permissions
sources.finding: Allow/ask/deny rules, durable project approvals and hard-deny policies are documented; shell uses host-user authority.

sources.title: OpenCode MCP servers
sources.finding: Local stdio and remote HTTP MCP clients support project/global config, OAuth and headers.

sources.title: OpenCode skills
sources.finding: Documents reusable instruction modules and their discovery.

sources.title: OpenCode desktop package
sources.locator: Main entry; Electron build and Solid dependencies
sources.finding: The pinned desktop build uses Electron and Solid.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/cli/web.mdx
sources.finding: OpenCode serves password-protected web UI from its runtime server. Pair links work once for five minutes; session cookies last 30 days and password change signs all out. Localhost is default; remote always-on hosts can use standalone serve under a supervisor. OpenTunnel remote exposure requires consent.

sources.title: OpenCode FAQ
sources.finding: OpenCode is explicitly free to use, includes free models without an account and can connect local models. Other providers may cost extra. Existing ChatGPT Plus/Pro and GitHub Copilot subscriptions are supported. Free-model data handling differs from other provider routes.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/claude-agent.mdx
sources.finding: Claude Agent runs installed Claude Code 2.1.248+ on the same machine using Claude login. OpenCode supplies tools/permissions/compaction/subagents; Claude Code hooks/MCP/settings/memory do not load. Not available in remote workspaces. Claude subscription costs show none; API routes use provider prices.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/cli/commands.mdx
sources.finding: CLI session export/import uses JSON with optional sanitize; stats exposes cost/tokens by model, time and project with JSON output. auth supports saved accounts and export/import credentials. Reload applies fresh services at next step boundary. acp starts a stdio server for editor integrations.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/tools.mdx
sources.finding: Read/glob/grep search files; webfetch/websearch retrieve external context. Subagent supports foreground results or background session IDs with continued prompts. Session and worktree utilities live in the Code Mode namespace; only worktree_remove requests a built-in permission (edit). Shell runs use host authority; no security-sandbox inference.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/plugins.mdx
sources.finding: Plugins load published packages or configured local directories plus discovered TS/JS files. CLI installs/checks/updates/removes plugins. Built-in policy/Console delivery plugins cannot be disabled by repository removal rules.

sources.title: OpenCode Workflow; Scope; Storage; Safety
sources.finding: Undo/redo stages conversation and file rollback using best-effort snapshots in local Git-object storage. File capture requires Git; outside Git only conversation rollback works. Ignored files, untracked files over 2 MiB and effects outside active directory are excluded. Rollback is not secure erasure or process/database rollback.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/console/members.mdx
sources.finding: Console owners/admins invite Members and change roles within own authority; last owner retained. Roles are Member/Admin/Owner. Invitations expire in seven days. Member removal revokes access and their workspace API keys immediately, while usage remains in reports. Go Teams invitation access costs separately.

sources.title: OpenCode services/site/src/docs/content/console/sso.mdx
sources.finding: Console workspaces include OIDC or SAML SSO, configured by owners. Admins/members must use it, including /connect; owners retain alternative login recovery. One connection per workspace. Domain verification/SCIM affect automatic membership.

sources.title: OpenCode V2 CLI CI workflow
sources.locator: run > CI; GitHub Actions example with on: [pull_request]
sources.finding: Official V2 CLI reference supplies a GitHub Actions pull_request-triggered workflow that installs @opencode/cli and runs opencode run --standalone with a provider key secret. GitHub Actions supplies the event/runner; this is a user-configured external workflow, not a built-in OpenCode scheduler.

sources.title: OpenCode browser session layout
sources.finding: The browser session model explicitly switches between desktop and narrow-screen layouts at 768px. The same password-protected web server powers the chat/session UI; it is a product client, not the public website.

sources.title: OpenCode subagent tool
sources.locator: Input/output schemas; child-session start/resume; foreground/background results
sources.finding: The product-owned subagent tool starts a child session with a configured agent and optional model, returns its session ID/result, and accepts follow-ups by sessionID. Background children notify the parent when complete. The OpenCode runtime supplies this coordinator tool.

sources.title: OpenCode Claude Agent execution boundary
sources.locator: How it works; packages/core/src/plugin/provider and tool/plugin
sources.finding: Claude Code is used for model calls and native login while OpenCode owns tools, permissions, compaction and subagents. The shipped provider registry includes this native Claude Agent integration; the other compared external coding harnesses are not supplied as session integrations. ChatGPT/Copilot/provider API routes are model access, not those harnesses.

sources.title: OpenCode supplied provider registry
sources.finding: The supplied plugins include the native Claude Agent plugin and model-provider API integrations. Bounded inspection found no supplied session adapter for Codex CLI, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI, Pi, Grok, Aider or Antigravity; ChatGPT, Copilot, Google and xAI provider names refer to model API access.

sources.title: OpenCode native Claude Code process and sessions
sources.locator: query-options.ts lines 59-104; claude/session.ts query; claude/sessions.ts resume
sources.finding: The shipped Claude Agent plugin passes the installed Claude executable and a spawner to the official Agent SDK, persists Claude sessions, resumes by saved Claude session ID and manages a long-running process per OpenCode session. It supplies OpenCode tools as MCP tools and disables Claude builtin tools/settings. This is native process/session management, beyond choosing an API model.

sources.title: OpenCode session todo implementation
sources.locator: Info/Input/Output schemas; tool execute metadata; core database/schema models
sources.finding: The experimental todowrite tool stores task content/status in a tool output and session metadata. The inspected native core schema/routes and tool implementation have no separate issue/backlog CRUD or cross-session work-item store; scheduled tasks are trigger configurations, not that backlog.

sources.title: OpenCode server authentication
sources.finding: The native server uses one fixed opencode username, a server password and password-derived pairing sessions. Multiple paired clients share that identity; this does not establish distinct human users jointly prompting an agent. Console billing/workspace membership is a separate scope.

sources.title: OpenCode optional Sentry initialization
sources.finding: Desktop/web Sentry initialization is gated by the build-time VITE_SENTRY_DSN. Inspection of the public native configuration did not establish an end-user control that disables telemetry in official desktop/web builds. V1 experimental.openTelemetry controls AI-SDK spans, a separate narrower instrument.

sources.title: OpenCode stable V1 GitHub Action
sources.finding: The publicly available stable V1 GitHub Action handles issue/PR comments, works on a branch and creates a GitHub pull request through octokit pulls.create. It is invoked through anomalyco/opencode/github@latest and is separate from the V2 native application.

sources.title: OpenCode V1 GitHub integration
sources.finding: The official maintained V1 documentation describes /opencode or /oc issue/PR comments launching GitHub Actions, implementing changes on a branch and submitting a PR. The page explicitly identifies itself as V1 documentation.

sources.title: OpenCode v2.3.0 release
sources.finding: The November 13 public V2.3 release changes subagents to always run in the background, return a session ID immediately and report to the parent whenever idle. This supersedes the optional foreground behavior in the separately pinned V2.2.6 tool source.
